description: Cross-references for California Penal Code § 502 computer fraud and unauthorized access

cross_references.title: 18 U.S.C. § 1030 — Computer Fraud and Abuse Act
cross_references.relationship: Federal parallel. § 502 provides state criminal and civil claims; CFAA provides federal criminal and civil claims. The two statutes apply simultaneously when the conduct has interstate character (which SIM swap attacks almost always do).

cross_references.title: 47 U.S.C. § 222 — CPNI
cross_references.relationship: The SIM swap that enables the § 502 unauthorized access starts with a § 222 CPNI violation at the carrier. The two violations are sequential: carrier fails → attacker gets access → unauthorized access occurs.

cross_references.title: California Penal Code § 530.5 — Identity Theft
cross_references.relationship: SIM swap is a method of identity theft. The § 502 computer fraud and § 530.5 identity theft charges are co-existing for the same SIM swap event.

cross_references.title: California Penal Code § 182 — Conspiracy
cross_references.relationship: If the SIM swap was coordinated by multiple actors (Christina + McClaran), § 182 conspiracy attaches to the § 502 substantive violations.

cross_references.title: California Civil Code § 3294 — Punitive Damages
cross_references.relationship: A § 502 violation committed with malice, oppression, or fraud (deliberately targeting the victim) supports a § 3294 punitive damages claim in the civil action.
